from PIL import Image
import numpy as np
import colorsys

a = np.asarray(img).astype(float)
col = a.mean(axis=0)
W = col.shape[0]
lum = col.mean(axis=1)

# 1) Orange / warm stripes: R > G > B with R-B large
r,g,b = col[:,0], col[:,1], col[:,2]
warm = (r - b > 25) & (r > g)
saturated = (col.max(axis=1) - col.min(axis=1) > 30)
print("warm stripe columns (frac of W):")
idx = np.where(warm & saturated)[0]
# group consecutive
groups=[]
if len(idx):
    s=idx[0]; p=idx[0]
    for i in idx[1:]:
        if i==p+1: p=i
        else: groups.append((s,p)); s=i; p=i
    groups.append((s,p))
for s,e in groups:
    c = col[s:e+1].mean(axis=0)
    print(f"  x={s/W:.3f}-{e/W:.3f}  rgb={c.round(1)}  lum={lum[s:e+1].mean():.1f}")

# 2) Teal / cyan stripes: B > R notably, G high-ish
teal = (b - r > 15) & (g > r) & (lum > 35)
idx = np.where(teal)[0]
groups=[]
if len(idx):
    s=idx[0]; p=idx[0]
    for i in idx[1:]:
        if i==p+1: p=i
        else: groups.append((s,p)); s=i; p=i
    groups.append((s,p))
print("teal-ish stripe groups (top by width):")
groups.sort(key=lambda t: -(t[1]-t[0]))
for s,e in groups[:12]:
    c = col[s:e+1].mean(axis=0)
    print(f"  x={s/W:.3f}-{e/W:.3f} w={e-s+1}  rgb={c.round(1)}")

# 3) Bright columns (lum > 120)
bright = lum > 120
idx = np.where(bright)[0]
groups=[]
if len(idx):
    s=idx[0]; p=idx[0]
    for i in idx[1:]:
        if i==p+1: p=i
        else: groups.append((s,p)); s=i; p=i
    groups.append((s,p))
print("bright groups (lum>120):", [(round(s/W,3), round(e/W,3)) for s,e in groups][:15])

# 4) profile of mean lum in 20 bins
bins = np.array_split(np.arange(W), 20)
for i,bi in enumerate(bins):
    c = col[bi].mean(axis=0)
    print(f"bin {i:2d} x={bi[0]/W:.2f}-{bi[-1]/W:.2f} rgb={c.round(1)} lum={c.mean():.1f}")
EOF

All the evidence converges on one film. Here's my analysis summary:

## Barcode signature
- **Near-colorless throughout**: mean saturation 0.036, essentially zero saturated red/blue/green anywhere — only 3 tiny warm blips (4.4%, 34.6%, 81%) and a handful of pale mint-teal stripes (8–30%, 43–47%)
- **Uniformly dark** (62% dark columns, peak segment brightness only ~lum 82), green-grey tint with blue always the lowest channel
- **Progressive darkening** through the final third, ending in ~12% pure black
- **Distinctive events**: neutral-grey overexposed run at ~33%, alternating dark/grey "strobe" blips at 40–47%, a dark red-orange blip at ~81%, one final warm blip at ~87.8% then black

## Why the others fail
- **Day of the Dead** — wall-to-wall blood red and bright saturated scenes; barcode has zero red
- **Exorcist III** — long bright-white dream sequences and a golden sunrise ending; nothing bright appears after 61% here
- **Apollo 18 / Boogeyman** — blue-tinted grades with wide bright bands; barcode is green-tinted with no bright bands
- **Nosferatu (1979)** — saturated forests, blue castle scenes, bright sunlit rides
- **Villains / Stonehearst / Wish Upon / Automata** — warm/bright palettes

## Why Silent House matches
Mapping content (0.8–88.1% of file) onto its 87-minute runtime, every feature lands on a documented scene: pale overcast opening (~0 min), warm lamp blip (~3.5 min), mint-teal window-lit walls and the teal-lit basement (~9–27 min), the **only outdoor stretch** — her escape through the cellar door into grey overcast daylight (~33 min, exactly the neutral-grey run), the famous **Polaroid-camera flash strobe sequence** (~40–47 min — the alternating dark/flash-lit grey blips), the teal-lit **bathtub hallucination** (~57 min), the **sledgehammer bludgeoning** as a dark red-brown blip in lamp light (~80 min), her silent walk-out (~87 min), then smash-cut to black for the credits. The real-time single-take structure also explains the smooth, cut-free color evolution and the steady dusk-to-night darkening, and the film's notoriously desaturated, pale-green-grey look matches the barcode's hue profile exactly.
